title: Where does a loaded ruler balance?
hook: A ruler with a lump on one end. Does it balance at the middle, the lump, or elsewhere?

knows: seesaws balance when the weights match
a ruler balances on its middle
doesNotKnow: the centre of mass as a mass-weighted average position

misconception: A uniform stick with a lump on it balances at its middle or right under the lump.
objective: The learner can explain that the balance point is the average position of all the mass, so a ruler and an equal lump balance halfway between the ruler's middle and the lump.

claims.text: The centre of mass is the mass-weighted average position: x = (sum of m x) / (sum of m).
claims.source: Definition; Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 9.

claims.text: A uniform ruler's own weight acts at its middle, 50 cm.
claims.source: Centre of mass of a uniform rod is at its midpoint by symmetry.

claims.text: With a 0.10 kg ruler and a 0.10 kg lump at 100 cm, the balance point is 75 cm.
A beam on a pivot balances when the turning effects on each side are equal (net torque zero); at 75 cm, 0.10 kg sits 25 cm to each side.
claims.source: Torque about the pivot: 0.10 g x (75 - 50) = 0.10 g x (100 - 75). Rigid beam, knife-edge pivot, no friction: stated in the code comment and the reveal.

claims.text: Off balance, the beam tips toward the side with the larger turning effect; the stage draws a fixed tip to a stop rather than a graded tilt.
claims.source: A rigid beam on a knife edge at its own level has no restoring torque; it tips until it meets a stop. The 8 degree tip angle is a drawing convention.

claims.text: A heavier lump pulls the balance point further toward it.
claims.source: x = (0.10 x 50 + m x 100) / (0.10 + m) increases with m toward 100 cm.

recall.question: A 2 kg plank, 4 m long, has a 2 kg toolbox on one end. How far from that end is its balance point?
recall.why: Equal masses at the middle (2 m from the end) and at the end average to halfway between them: 1 m from the toolbox end.
